Headquartered in London, ORCA has delivered eleven on-premises quantum computers worldwide – demonstrating that its technology is not theoretical but already delivering real world results.

At the core of ORCA’s innovation is its hybrid quantum-classical architecture, engineered for seamless integration into existing AI and HPC infrastructure. Its current PT-2 system, a rack-mounted quantum computer, connects directly to GPU clusters via NVIDIA’s CUDA-Q platform, enabling accelerated AI workloads with significantly lower energy consumption than traditional silicon-based systems. Backed by a strong portfolio of patent families spanning photonic integrated circuits, quantum memory, and multiplexing technologies, ORCA is enabling enterprises, research institutions, and HPC operators to unlock new levels of performance, efficiency, and scalability.

As ORCA prepares to launch its next-generation PT-3 system, the company is entering a pivotal phase of growth and technological advancement. Its solutions are already being embedded into generative AI pipelines, delivering measurable improvements in model performance, while also addressing the rising energy demands of large-scale AI adoption. With a focus on practical deployment and a clear roadmap to fault-tolerant quantum computing, ORCA is leading the development and deployment of quantum technology, providing a commercially viable path to the future of computing.

**What will you do**

This is a hands-on hardware engineering role at the heart of ORCA’s R&D team, working directly on the development of the PT-Series – our photonic quantum computing platform designed to accelerate AI and machine learning workloads. You’ll work across the full hardware development cycle, from early concept through to validated, production-ready designs, collaborating closely with physicists, optical engineers, and software developers to bring genuinely novel hardware to life.

* Design and develop analogue and mixed-signal circuitry for precision quantum photonic hardware, covering signal conditioning, low-noise amplification, DAC interfaces, and driver electronics for opto-electronic components.
* Own the PCB design process for your modules: schematic capture, layout, design review, and iteration through to a working, characterised board.
* Work hands-on in the lab: characterise your designs using oscilloscopes, spectrum analysers, signal generators, and other bench equipment to verify performance and debug issues systematically.
* Collaborate with the software team to define hardware/software interfaces and support integration of your electronics into the wider PT-Series system.
* Support EMC and regulatory compliance work as hardware matures toward product-ready status.
* Document your designs thoroughly: schematics, test reports, design reviews, and specifications so the wider team can build on your work.
* Work cross-functionally with physics, optics, and software teams to understand system-level requirements and translate them into practical electronic designs.

**What will you bring – required**

* A degree in electronic engineering, electrical engineering, physics, or a closely related discipline.
* 2 – 4 years of professional experience in hardware or electronics engineering (industry experience preferred; strong academic laboratory research will also be considered).
* Solid understanding of analogue and mixed-signal design principles: amplification, filtering, signal conditioning, low-noise techniques, and ADC/DAC interfacing.
* Hands-on PCB design experience, including simulation, schematic capture and layout using tools such as SPICE, Altium Designer, KiCAD, or equivalent.
* Comfortable using standard bench instruments to bring up, debug, and characterise electronic hardware.
* Some experience with or understanding of embedded firmware and microcontroller-based systems.
* A methodical, practical approach to design and debugging, you run structured experiments, follow the data, and iterate with purpose.

**Nice to have**

* Exposure to RF design fundamentals: impedance matching, transmission lines, RF signal conditioning.
* Familiarity with EMC testing or compliance processes (CE marking, UKCA, or similar).
* Experience integrating electronics with opto-electronic or photonic systems.

**Who we are looking for**

* Ownership mindset: You take designs from concept to validated hardware and care about the outcome at every step — not just your schematic, but whether the system works end-to-end.
* Hands-on curiosity: You’re most comfortable with an oscilloscope probe in one hand and a design question in the other. You enjoy the lab as much as the desk.
* Collaborative by nature: You work well alongside physicists, optical engineers, and software developers who don’t all speak the same technical language. Translating between disciplines energises you rather than frustrating you.
* Bias toward action: You iterate quickly, run structured tests to isolate problems, and don’t wait to be told when something needs attention.
* Attention to detail: You understand that in precision quantum hardware, the difference between a good design and a great one often comes down to layout decisions, grounding choices, and the trade-offs that aren’t visible until bring-up.

**Why join us**

Joining ORCA Computing offers the opportunity to work at the forefront of quantum technology, where innovation is already delivering real-world impact. Across commercial, operational, and product roles, you’ll collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to bring advanced quantum systems to market and help integrate quantum capabilities into modern AI and data centre ecosystems.

ORCA provides a rare chance to contribute to a pivotal moment in the evolution of computing. With a culture built on ownership, collaboration, and ambition, the company empowers individuals to solve complex challenges and shape how next-generation quantum technologies are developed, deployed, and scaled across industries – driving a more efficient and powerful future for AI and compute.

PATH is a global nonprofit dedicated to achieving health equity. With more than 40 years of experience forging multisector partnerships and with expertise in science, economics, technology, advocacy, and dozens of other specialties, PATH develops and scales up innovative solutions to the world’s most pressing health challenges. 


About AI for Health 

PATH’s Artificial Intelligence (AI) Initiative is our flagship technical team working across divisions to deliver best-in-class evaluation and implementation of AI in health, spanning model evaluation to product development and service innovation. We aim to use AI to address the world’s largest health inequities. 

We’re looking for a clinician with research experience to help deliver PATH’s work evaluating whether different AI models and products can provide safe and effective mental health/wellbeing support for those most in need. You will collaborate with leading AI evaluation labs and with clinical, research, lived experience, and policy experts across sub-Saharan Africa and the UK to develop new ways of contextualising evaluation so that we can better understand what works, for whom, and in which contexts. You’ll bring clinical expertise to the design and execution of our evaluations, as well as coordinate day-to-day delivery across an international consortium. This role is a strong fit for an early-career clinical psychologist or medical doctor with a demonstrated interest in psychiatry who wants their work to change how AI is built and used for mental health. 

Responsibilities:

Bring Clinical Expertise to Evaluation 

Contribute to evaluation design, including which AI systems we test, who we test them for, how we test them, and how we learn from our partners to refine our approach. Keep this all current as the field evolves. 
Ground our simulated users/patients and automated (LLM) judges in clinical practice: help our partners specify personas and presentations and draft behaviour rubrics, and review transcripts for clinical errors before they go to the panels of clinicians and lived experience experts in each country. Expect to work hands-on alongside our partners. 
Lead PATH’s evaluation of consumer AI products, from general-purpose assistants to dedicated mental health apps, while tailoring evaluations to specific populations, cultures, and languages. Coordinate with developers on evaluation of their models and products. 
Co-author research on new methods for contextualised AI evaluation with consortium partners, bringing clinical expertise to how we build and validate simulated users/patients and LLM-judges. 

Coordinate Delivery across the Consortium

Matrix manage members of the AI4Health team supporting the delivery of consumer AI product evaluations, including both fellows doing their PhDs (whom you will contribute to the supervision of), as well as peers leading engineering for the programme. 
Contribute to donor reports and to presentations for funders and external audiences. 

Publish Evidence

Prepare content for a website presenting all results of PATH’s AI evaluations in mental health, including plain-language summaries for people seeking support; contribute to writing seminal reports on the state of AI safety and effectiveness for global mental health; and support presentation of evidence to international commissions and panels. 
Write up our results for high-impact academic venues and established policy fora. 

Contribute to the Broader AI programme 

Support research and related activities led by other members of the AI team (where your expert skill set is relevant, and sometimes just as another pair of hands), including the soon-to-be-launched ‘Nature Commission on Consumer AI and Wellbeing’ for which PATH is hosting the secretariat. 
This is a full-time post based in London. You’ll report to PATH’s Deputy Director for AI for Health. This role includes international travel to partner sites and convenings (around 10–15% of time). 


Required Skills and Experience 


Qualification as a clinical psychologist (DClinPsy or equivalent), or as a medical doctor with experience of, or a clear interest in, psychiatry. 
At least two years’ clinical experience since qualifying as a clinical psychologist or doctor. 
Research experience, with evidence of scientific writing (e.g., publications, preprints, or a doctoral thesis). 
Expertise/experience in measurement and evaluation methods—reliability, validity, inter-rater agreement. 
Some programming experience (e.g., Python or R), and hands-on use of LLMs (e.g., writing prompts, or writing and testing rubrics). 
Excellent written and verbal communication for scientific, clinical, public, and policy audiences. 
Ability to coordinate work and deadlines across complex, multi-stakeholder projects. 

Preferred Qualifications 

Research experience in digital mental health or experience evaluating digital health products (including their clinical safety). 
Experience working with collaborators or patients in low- and middle-income countries, ideally in sub-Saharan Africa. 
Experience coordinating a multi-partner or multi-site research program. 
Research experience in simulating users or patients with LLMs, validating automated judges against human raters, or building LLM-based evaluation pipelines. 
Experience of industry engagement and/or evaluation governance. 
Experience working with lived experience or patient and public involvement panels.

# Growth Strategy and Operations Analyst at Penfold

**Hi, we’re Penfold - we’re on a mission to help everyone save enough to be comfortable in later life! 🚀**

There’s over a trillion pounds sitting in UK pensions – but most of it is with legacy providers offering outdated products and poor service. We’re here to change that.

Penfold is building the pension of the future – a modern, tech-first platform that makes saving for later life easy, engaging and accessible for everyone.

We’re a growing team of 70+ builders across London and Tallinn, backed by some of the world’s leading FinTech investors. Having raised £25M+, we manage £1bn+ in pensions for over 100,000 savers and thousands of businesses — and we’re on track for profitability next year.

As one of our first 90 hires, you’ll play a key role in shaping our culture and have loads of opportunity to grow, progress and make your mark.

**About the role**

We are building a small, dedicated growth team, and this is a new role within it. The team is responsible for growing the value of the pensions our members hold with us, and increasing membership through the Refer-a-Friend programme.

The role covers several areas across a member’s pension journey, from the point they join us through to long after they leave an employer.

You would report to the Head of Growth, who is accountable for the growth numbers themselves. Your job would be to make sure the team is aiming at the right things, that the numbers it relies on can be trusted, and that decisions get made on evidence.

**Your responsibilities**

**Analysis and direction**

* Use cohort and funnel data to work out how to maximise post-acquisition customer value
* Turn that analysis into specific recommendations for colleagues about who to contact, and why
* Use AI tools and automation where they help you reach an answer faster, particularly for exploratory analysis
* Maintain the framework the team uses to measure growth, and work out what the underlying dashboards need to show

**Forecasting and sizing**

* Build and maintain the forecast for the growth function
* Size new growth ideas before they are pursued, so effort goes toward the highest impact ones
* Write the business case for larger initiatives

**Experiment design**

* Design experiments properly with clear hypotheses, agreed ways of judging success, and appropriate holdout groups
* Interpret results and ensure they reflect genuine effects
* Write up what was learned after each significant test, along with a view on what should happen next

**Coordination and reporting**

* Support the Head of Growth in coordinating the planning and follow-up for the team’s initiatives each quarter, most of which are cross-functional
* Growth PMO support – keeping track of who owns what and by when, and flagging early if something is falling behind schedule
* Support the Head of Growth in producing the regular reporting the wider business sees on how growth is progressing

**Skills and Experience:**

**Must-haves**

* 2-4 years in a role such as revenue operations, management consulting, strategy, or growth / product analytics - ideally somewhere that was growing quickly
* A strong analytical toolkit: highly capable with spreadsheet modelling; and experience working with AI for deep analysis, and BI tools such as QuickSight, Looker or Tableau
* A first-principles approach to problems: the ability to take an ambiguous situation apart, question the assumptions built into it, and arrive at a model, a number and a recommendation
* A working understanding of experiment design: holdouts, sample size, and how to judge whether a result reflects a real effect
* Clear communication: the ability to explain your thinking in writing and in person, and to make a case to someone senior, calmly, when the evidence supports it.
* A tendency to see things through: you take an idea, do the work to move it forward, and follow up without needing to be chased

**Nice-to-haves**

* Some exposure to pensions, financial services, payroll or workplace benefits, or another regulated industry with both business and consumer customers
* Experience with dbt or a similar data warehouse, and with tools used for running experiments, such as Statsig
* Familiarity with CRM or lifecycle marketing platforms, and how marketing attribution works.
* Exposure to a business where teams are measured against commercial targets.

### **What We’re Looking For**

This role suits someone who takes a considered, evidence-led approach to a commercial problem. You will probably recognise yourself if:

* You back up a recommendation with a model and a number
* You can take a vague, messy problem, work out what is actually being asked, and get to a clear answer
* You know how to set up an experiment properly, and can tell when a result is worth trusting
* You are comfortable coordinating work that spans several teams at once
* You care whether your analysis actually changes what the team does next

Be prepared to work hard! Ultimately, we’re looking for smart, hardworking & energetic people who get stuff done & are committed to contributing to a great team. So, if you’re excited about what we’re doing, get in touch – definitely don’t be put off if you don’t tick every box! 

### **Our application process:**

* Intro Call (30 mins) – get to know Penfold and briefly discuss your experience.
* Experience Deep-Dive (45 - 60 mins) – walk through a piece of work you have owned; discuss your approach, your results, and how you work day to day
* Take-Home Task (max 120 mins) – to see how you structure a problem, reach a number, and explain it.
* Task Review + discussion (60 mins)
* Culture Fit (up to 45 mins with 3 people from other departments)

### **Benefits:**

We’re working hard to create a working environment where people feel empowered to do their very best work, make a big impact, and enjoy what they do. Specifically, our benefits package includes:

* A competitive salary; we proactively review salaries to make sure you get what you deserve
* Meaningful share options, you’ll own a part of Penfold and share in our success
* 10% pension contribution each month that you don’t need to match (on top of your salary)
* Medical insurance, through Vitality
* Unlimited holiday, we’re interested in your output, not how many holidays you go on!
* Hybrid working, we like people to come in to our office (so it would be great if you lived in the London area) at least a couple of days a week to collaborate, but we trust you to get your work done in whatever environment suits you
* Great community office space, plenty of people come into our wonderful private office near Borough Underground station.
* Free tea, coffee, soft drinks and snacks
* Free company lunch every week (e.g., Borough Market, Mercato Metropolitano)
* Laptop and any WFH equipment you need
* Option to buy a bike tax free, and spread the cost (using the cycle to work scheme)
* Learning and Professional Development – we conduct regular 360 feedback and focus on role progression that suits each individual. We support everyone with courses, events and coaching to help everyone reach their goals
* Quarterly company socials, and regular meet-ups throughout the year too!
* Plus a host of other benefits – **see here: https://getpenfold.com/careers**

—

Would you like to create the future of a product used by thousands of businesses and millions of consumers? In a typical month, Phorest processes 3 million appointments and we send over 3 million SMS and 4 million emails. We process 200k online bookings per month and over 150 custom built white label native apps.

#### **The Opportunity**

We’re adding to our security capability and we are looking for someone who can move the needle, not a ticket-taker, but an experienced engineer who takes initiative, builds things, and genuinely partners with our product and engineering teams and the wider business. You’ll use your deep security expertise not only to solve complex problems, but to raise the security capability of the teams around you.

Reactive work eats into time that should be spent on proactive, strategic programmes. You will change that dynamic: by building security tooling and processes that scale, identifying risks and capability gaps, and turning them into impactful improvements. By embedding yourself in our engineering culture you’ll make security an integral part of how teams build and enable engineers to make good security decisions.

You will function primarily as an enabler, working across our stream-aligned engineering teams to build security knowledge, tooling, and practice where the work actually happens. An integral part of your impact will come through coaching others, sharing knowledge and creating scalable practices that raise the security bar for our Engineering Team.

#### **What You'll Do**

You will own security engineering outcomes - acting as SME, identifying cross-functional opportunities, and driving improvements through to impact.

**Security Platform & Developer Tooling**

* Partner with engineering teams to introduce tooling that makes secure coding the path of least resistance. Identify opportunities to improve the security experience and take ownership of delivering improvements that materially reduce risk or friction.
* Collaborate with platform engineers to weave security into CI/CD pipelines, our cloud environment and code review workflows, without creating friction or bottlenecks. Establish reusable patterns and practices that enable teams to adopt secure-by-default approaches.
* Work with engineering leads to identify and prioritise process & tooling improvements against our real risk landscape, building shared agreement on what matters most.

**Developer Enablement & Partnership**

* Proactively identify security knowledge and capability gaps, and build confidence across Phorest engineering through collaborative threat-modelling sessions, documentation, and hands-on pairing, so teams can make good security decisions independently.
* Embed with stream-aligned product teams at key stages like design, architecture review, pre-launch to provide security input as a trusted peer, not an external auditor. Coach teams through complex security decisions, helping them build their own capability.
* Act as a subject matter expert and trusted partner between Security and Product & Engineering, helping teams understand security and compliance requirements.
* Share security learnings, emerging threats and lessons from incidents across Engineering, creating reusable guidance that raises the baseline of secure engineering and proactively creates awareness for how teams consider security.

**Security Monitoring & Risk Understanding**

* Work alongside the broader security and IT team to proactively monitor security signals and alerts, identify patterns and build shared situational awareness across the team.

# Staff Engineer - Business Spend

## Location

United Kingdom; Denmark; Portugal; Spain

## Employment Type

Full time

## Location Type

Remote

## Department

Engineering

## Deadline to Apply

October 13, 2026 at 1:00 AM PDT

OverviewApplication

## **About Pleo**

Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.

The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.

Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

## **About the role**

**Please note: applications will be open until Tuesday 13th October 2026 at 08.00 CEST.**  
**We will not review any applications before the closing window so please don't rush to apply and use the time to submit a high quality application.**

We're looking for a Staff Engineer to join the Business Spend segment at Pleo. In this role, you'll help us build invoices, purchase orders, supplier invoices, cards for subscriptions and be part of Business Spend as we scale procurement to pay services. If you're excited about systems with real history and are passionate about building services that handle what a company spends to run itself, then this is the opportunity for you!

## **Who you’ll be working with and reporting to**

You’ll report to our Engineering Manager in Business Spend and work closely with teams in accounting systems and card infrastructure. Our team of 10 is highly collaborative and dedicated to invoices and vendors. You’ll also have the chance to partner with teams across product, design and compliance to ensure success.

## **What you’ll be doing**

As a Staff Engineer, you will:

* Partner with the Engineering Manager to own and be accountable for the whole architecture of Business Spend.
* Own significant parts of our supplier data migration, moving supplier and bank account logic out of a legacy service into a dedicated one, per customer and without downtime.
* Improve the reliability of our invoice payment flows, where roughly 2.5% of payments currently fail and every failure is a customer who can't pay a supplier.
* Turn our new vendor data model into working software, so that a supplier means the same thing across cards, invoices, and accounting.
* Help the 3 teams make consistent technical decisions, through design documents, code review, and the architecture forum, without being anyone's manager.
* Raise the people around you, through pairing, review, and writing things down clearly enough that someone in another time zone can act on them.

To put things into context, here's what's on our roadmap right now: extracting supplier management out of our legacy invoice service, meeting the ISO 20022 structured address requirements for outbound payments, and rebuilding how we model suppliers and vendors across the whole of Business Spend.

On the technical side, you can expect to work with the following stack: AWS, Github actions, Kotlin on the JVM, Kafka, Spring Boot, Gradle, Kubernetes, and Grafana for metrics, logs, and traces. Our frontend is TypeScript and React.

## **What you bring**

You’ll thrive in this role if you have:

* Strong verbal communication. You can hold a room of engineers who don't share a first language and leave everyone clear on what was decided.
* Experience as the technical lead for a team spread across several countries and time zones. You adapt how you communicate rather than expecting everyone to adapt to you, and you're as effective in writing and async as you are live.
* Deep backend engineering experience in a modern statically typed language such as Java, Kotlin or TypeScript, on systems running in production at scale.
* A track record of shipping inside a legacy system that was being taken apart. Not just designing the target state, but doing the migration.
* The ability to change technical direction across teams you don't own, with specific examples of when you've done it.
* Writing that other people can act on. Design documents, decision records, migration plans that work without you in the room.
* A background in payments, fintech, accounts payable, ERP or B2B SaaS.
* Experience with event-driven systems and Kafka, and a habit of building observability into what you ship.

## **Why is this role a good fit for you**

This role is a good fit for you if:

* You want to work on a genuinely unsolved problem. How a company models its suppliers across cards, invoices, and accounting is the hardest open question in our product, and we're answering it this year.
* You want your work to be visible. The team is small enough that one person changes the outcome, and you'll see the effect on customers within weeks.
* You like being the person others come to, and you'd rather earn that through the work than be handed it in a job title.

This role is not a good fit for you if:

* You want a green field project. You'll spend a real share of your time in code you didn't write, with constraints you didn't choose.
* You want to design the target state and hand it over. Here you design it and then you build it.
* You need formal authority to get things moving. You'll need to rely on technical influence and earn trust across 3 teams.

## **How you’ll develop in this role**

In your first 6 months at Pleo, you will:

* Take ownership of a major workstream in the supplier migration and carry it to production.
* Work with the Accounts Payable team to improve payment reliability and the observability behind it.
* Build the relationships across all 3 teams that make cross-team technical work possible, and grow into a larger share of the architecture direction for Business Spend.

We're committed to helping you develop your career. For this role, that means a growing share of technical direction across the segment, and a clear conversation about what the next level looks like and what it takes to get there. We'd rather have that conversation early than have you find the answer somewhere else.

Please note: We can hire on a remote, hybrid or in-person set-up in any of the locations listed on the advert but you will need to be physically based in the country of your choice with a valid right to work. We are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role in any of the listed locations.

## **Show me the benefits**

* Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!)
* Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office
* Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis
* 25 days of annual leave + public holidays (additional days may apply in select countries based on local standards).
* For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options
* We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far
* Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work

## **The interview process**

We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:

1. Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background.
2. Hiring Manager interview: A 60-minute experience-based conversation to deep dive into technical leadership experience, achievements and complexity you’ve been used to.
3. Core skills test: A 75-minute system-design interview with two of our engineers to deep dive into your architecture and problem solving skills.
4. Pleo challenge: A 60-minute presentation interview focusing on discussing one of your previous achievements.
5. Final interview: A 45-minute leadership interview assessing your behavioural skills and values.

Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success!

Last time we hired a Staff Engineer, we received a total of 1258 applications but only 8 were selected for an intro call. With this in mind, we want to help you understand what we really care about when reviewing your application:

* We receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI - it’s a big focus for us internally too- but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you - not AI - know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background.
* Every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process.
* The Staff seniority level at Pleo requires to have extensive experience operating as a technical lead / owner of initiatives that have cross team / domain impact in SaaS organisations of 500+ people. We’re also looking for someone with significant experience architecting services across multiple domains (e.g. invoicing, subscription cards etc.) and with the ability to decouple complex legacy systems through an effective long-term delivery plan. If you do not have this experience, please do not apply. If you do have this experience, please ensure your CV truly reflects it.

## **About your application**

* **English first.** Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us.
* **A fair look for everyone.** Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails.
* **Diversity drives us.** We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us.
* **Interview at your best.** We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email belonging@pleo.io. We’ll design a process that works for you.
* **Your data is safe.** When you apply, we process your personal data as a data processor. For more information on how Pleo processes personal data, read our Privacy Policy here.
* **Applying for multiple roles?** Nothing is stopping you, and we assess every role independently. However, we do look for alignment, so make sure you can explain why your interest and experience are right for each specific role.
* **Reapplying.** If you’re applying for the same role again, please wait six months from your last decision before hitting submit.

At Productboard, we're building the first agentic product management system. We're rethinking how product management is done in a world full of AI agents, and how we help our customers build what matters for their audience. AI is changing what an interface even is: static screens are giving way to conversations, generated artifacts, rich interactive UI, and open-ended workflows, often on the same screen.

We're looking for a **Principal Product Designer to be the UX architect of the product:** a hands-on senior IC from an AI-first product company **who defines the architecture and patterns that make Productboard one coherent, AI-first product** rather than a collection of independently designed experiences, sets its design direction, raises the bar for design, usability, and UX architecture across every product team, and personally carries the hardest design work.

This is a role with organization-wide scope and real decision rights, and partnering closely with Product, Engineering, and the Product Executive team. You'll decide how agentic workflows meet a structured product: how Spark's work lands in a purpose-built data model, visualizations, and documents, when a task should be a conversation, a generated artifact, or a conventional interface, and which of those patterns become product-wide standards. You'll make sure agents, artifacts, and structured UI hold together as one experience, and set a higher bar for everything that ships: coherent, usable end to end, and built on one architecture. Our users are product makers themselves. They can tell in the first minute whether a product was made with care, and design is how we win that minute.

## Your responsibilities

* **Own Productboard's UX and interaction architecture.** The information architecture, navigation model, and object model that make Productboard feel like one product. As Spark, our AI agent for product teams, reshapes what the product does, decide how new capabilities fit into that structure instead of becoming isolated features, and spot when a local decision will fragment the whole.
* **Define the interaction patterns for an AI-first product.** How users meet Spark, build trust in its output, delegate to it, and stay in control. Decide when an experience should be chat, rich interactive UI, a generated artifact, or a conventional interface, and how AI-generated outputs turn into actionable work. Nobody has cracked this yet. Define our answer so we build differentiated AI experiences, not AI features bolted onto an old interaction model.
* **Decide what becomes standard.** Which patterns teams adopt, evolve, or retire, and how design-system principles are interpreted across product domains. Codify them so teams decide faster, land on the same answer, and the bar rises everywhere at once, and so you can say of any pattern: this is the agreed pattern, this is why it works, and this is how every team applies it.
* **Set the design direction and design language.** Define what Productboard looks and behaves like as one product: the visual language, the interaction vocabulary, and the principles designers work from. Connect user insight, product strategy, and long-term vision into a direction the org can follow, and bring architecture and usability to the executive table with evidence.
* **Raise the bar for end-to-end usability and cross-product coherence.** Define what highly usable means at Productboard, continuously evaluate core product flows against it, and call it when a proposed experience is inconsistent, unclear, or below the usability bar. Drive the fixes across team boundaries. You are accountable for the end-to-end usability and consistency of what ships, and your findings feed the quality call on every launch.
* **Be the lead voice in design critique.** You are the person in the room who catches when a detail breaks the model, and the person designers come to when a pattern is unclear or a problem doesn't fit the architecture. Give domain designers strong architectural guidance and develop senior and staff designers through pairing and coaching. You're their architect, not their manager.
* **Personally carry the hardest design work.** Platform-level and foundational problems: the navigation model, object model redesigns, new surfaces, and new interaction primitives for human-agent collaboration. Own them from concept to coded prototype to shipped.
* **Prototype in code by default.** When words aren't settling a design debate, build the thing with AI coding tools. Turn ambiguous interaction and system questions into working prototypes, test them with users, and use them to align stakeholders and unblock engineering.

## About you

* **8+ years in product design as a senior individual contributor** on complex products, ideally in product-led B2B SaaS with a mature design practice. You have never stopped designing, and your portfolio has recent work in it.
* **Systems thinker:** you see a product as a whole, its object model, information architecture, and how the parts relate, and you can hold that structure in your head while designing a single detail within it. Concept models, sitemaps, and flows are second nature, not extra deliverables.
* **Proven bar raiser:** you've owned the usability of an entire product, not a feature, and there's a product that is visibly more coherent and more usable because you were there.
* **Agentic systems experience:** you've designed products where an agent does real work on the user's behalf and the design problem is trust, control, and cold start, across chat, generated artifacts, and rich UI, not just one of them. You have real opinions on how these products should fit into structured UI, because you use the newest ones the week they ship.
* **AI-first role model:** AI agents are how you work, every day, for research, prototyping, building, and analysis. When a debate needs settling, you build a working prototype with Claude Code, Cursor, or whatever fits. Code is a means for you, not the identity.
* **Excellent craft:** your interaction and visual design are at a level where senior designers want your feedback, and you've set a design language others were glad to work in.
* **Comfortable owning the call:** you've set standards for teams that weren't yours, made the unpopular consistency call, and made it stick with reasoning and evidence rather than rank.
* **Earned a seat at the roadmap:** PMs and executives come to you for direction, not just design, because your understanding of users is deep enough to shape what gets built.
* **Self-directed and evidence-driven:** you identify what needs to be done and do it, land into teams gracefully, and collaborate with low ego. You balance intuition from years of experience with strategy, data, and measurement. Intuition opens the question, evidence closes it.
* **Strategic communicator:** you can align executives around a design direction with the same clarity you bring to critiquing a designer's prototype, and you build trust across Product, Engineering, and Design.

* **Be the UX architect of the first agentic product management system,** a category being defined right now, where the patterns you set become the reference others copy.
* **Hold real decision rights over an entire product's UX** and use them to raise the bar for its architecture, patterns, and usability, with the mandate and executive partnership to actually change it.

Agents work faster, cheaper and more reliably when they write code instead of making one tool call at a time. That code needs somewhere safe to run. Monty is our answer: a Python interpreter written from scratch in Rust, with no filesystem, environment or network, that starts in under a millisecond and can be paused, dumped to bytes and resumed later. Monty is open source and reached 1.0 in September. Full Monty is the commercial product that runs the same sandbox behind a WebSocket, distributed as a container image.

We're looking for a senior Rust engineer to work directly with our founder, Samuel Colvin, on both. Roughly 60% of the work is on open source Monty and the rest on the commercial product. * Build and run the commercial product: production reliability, scaling, and the operational work of a service customers pay for.

Wholesale is a $50 trillion market still working the way it did in 1950. 90% of transactions happen offline, over calls, catalogues and trade shows, and a product passes through four or five layers of distributors and wholesalers before it reaches a store, with every party deciding on a fraction of the picture. By the time it hits the shelf, it costs roughly 40% more than the maker charged. That inefficiency tax runs into the trillions, and everyone pays it every time they buy anything.

Qogita is building the operating system that replaces that chain, which makes the product the core of what we are building. Every job of the traditional supply chain gets done once rather than at every layer, by a self-learning system rather than by hand: a buyer who used to deal with twenty suppliers gets an instant basket assembled from every available seller, forecasting reads what is actually selling in every market as it sells, and goods move straight from seller to retailer on the cheapest and fastest route. No part of it stands alone. The order book, the demand planner and the logistics network are each worth more combined with the others, every layer has to be machine-readable and actionable by agents as well as people, and every transaction writes a record that sharpens the next price, allocation and route. Deciding what to build, in what order, and which steps to skip entirely is the product problem, and it is already working: 95% of transactions involve no human touch, AI agents resolve over 90% of unique issues with zero human intervention, and the business is doubling every year.

The role

Most European wholesale still runs on PDF price lists, WhatsApp threads and payment terms designed to squeeze whoever has the least cash. Nobody designed that. It accumulated, and it's still how most of a very large industry works.

We're hiring one Senior Product Manager to own a hard part of replacing it. You'll take a single surface end to end: what gets built, why, and whether the number moved afterwards. There is no roadmap waiting for you and nobody is going to write your specs.

Depending on your strengths, that surface is likely to be one of the following:

 * The autonomous procurement layer: agents that watch price movements across thousands of supplier feeds, forecast demand, raise purchase orders and handle routine supplier email. Most of the straightforward operational work is already automated. The open question is the rest of it, and what has to be true about accuracy and auditability before software is allowed to commit company money.
 * Price and supply intelligence: we can see pricing, availability and demand across this market in a way no individual participant can. Whether that stays an internal tool or becomes something brands and large buyers pay for is genuinely undecided.
 * Catalogue and trust: matching, deduplication, authenticity and supplier reliability scoring across hundreds of thousands of SKUs. Nobody will congratulate you for it, and everything else depends on it.
 * Buyer economics: financing, terms, replenishment and retention. The levers that decide whether an independent retailer is still trading in five years.

 * Own the strategy, the specs and the outcome for your area, and be the person accountable when the metric doesn't move
 * Work from what's economically and physically true: units, margins, lead times, cash cycles, failure rates. "That's how marketplaces do it" isn't an argument here. A lot of industry convention is old error nobody went back and re-examined
 * Try to delete the thing before you build it. Every screen, field and integration is something a person maintains for years. Removing ten workflows is usually worth more than shipping an eleventh
 * Question whether a process should exist before you automate it, otherwise you get the same waste faster and buried in code
 * Do your own analysis. The warehouse is open and you won't be queuing behind an analyst to find out whether your idea worked
 * Bring the number, the sample size and the reason you might be wrong. Changing your mind publicly when the data turns against you counts in your favour here
 * Go and look at the actual thing: sit with ops, listen to supplier calls, read the orders that failed. Judgement built only from dashboards decays quickly
 * Work directly with engineers, designers, data scientists and the commercial teams, in the room, at pace. We ship weekly and make reversible decisions in hours

 * 5+ years in product
 * You've shipped things that moved a number you can name at a scale you can defend, and you can explain why it worked rather than telling the version of the story where it obviously would
 * You're properly numerate and comfortable in SQL. You can put a rough figure on an outcome before you build it, and you're usually within an order of magnitude
 * You understand systems and data models well enough that engineers take you seriously in your first week. You don't need to be an engineer
 * You'll argue hard in the room and then commit to whatever we land on, including when we land against you
 * If something's broken and nobody owns it, you own it now
 * You're neither breathless nor dismissive about agents doing commercial work with limited supervision. It isn't a feature, it's a different risk model, and we want someone with judgement about it

# **Function: Data Management**

Data Management involves the collection, cleaning & storing of clinical trial data, utilizing a variety of industry and/or inhouse products and tools. Data Management safeguards data integrity, ensuring patient safety and the quality of data used to support decision-making in drug development. We are offering positions in 3 areas within Data Management:

## **Role: Data Quality Lead**

DQLs oversee the quality, integrity, and availability of clinical trial data, ensuring it is fit for purpose and ready for analysis by our statisticians. Working with multiple functions, DQLs manage the design and implementation of the study database, and oversee data collection and data cleaning strategies. As a DQL, you will be a key member of the clinical study team, and your ​day to day work will be divided between​ data and people - solving novel data problems, but also learning to lead & influence others​.

* Pursuing a degree in Data Science, Life Sciences, or a related field

Technical Excellence acts as the key link between the clinical data management team and technical Informatics (IT) colleagues. Functional Excellence Specialists play a key role in helping our Data Management group improve how we manage clinical trial data by bridging the gap between new technology and the people who use it. This non-technical role focuses on change management, and making processes more efficient, consistent and scalable.

You will gain hands-on experience in knowledge management, and learn how to improve the quality and longevity of our tools, ensuring they effectively support our colleagues in their day to day work.

**Who You are**

Analytical Data Scientists (ADS) are responsible for providing analytical and programming expertise for the reporting and analysis of clinical trials and related submissions to Health Authorities worldwide. We work closely with other members of Data Sciences, in particular biostatistics and data management, to ensure quality and integrity of study data. We also collaborate with other functional experts to determine appropriate analysis of data for respective disease areas. 

## **Role: DSX (Data Science Acceleration) Data Scientist**

The Data Science Acceleration (DSX) team is responsible for developing scalable data engineering and analytical tools, environments, and workflows that enable efficient, high-quality statistical computing across Product Development Data Sciences and Analytics (PDD). They focus on creating and maintaining next-generation capabilities that support automation of programming workflows, generation of reusable coding macros, and advanced data visualization.

**Who You Are (applies to both Analytical Data Sciences roles)**

* Pursuing a degree in Mathematics, Data Science, Bioinformatics, Computer Science, Statistics, or a related quantitative or computational field
* Good problem solving and logical thinking skills, as well as a keen interest in analytics
* Knowledge of some programming languages (R, SAS, Python) beneficial

# **Function: Biostatistics**

As a trusted analytical partner in drug development, Biostatistics provides strategic leadership and drives data-led decision making to bring safe, effective medicines to patients faster.  We are responsible for designing robust clinical trials and analysis plans that safeguard data integrity, ensure regulatory compliance, and maximise the statistical success rate of our studies. Our team operates at the frontline of the industry by identifying opportunities to implement innovative statistical methods across the wider organization. We are offering 1 position within biostatistics.

## **Role: Biostatistician**

Statisticians use their statistical expertise to design, analyse and interpret the results of clinical trials. We are a key member of cross functional teams, working closely with both technical (data management, statistical programming) and non-technical (clinical science, safety science, regulatory) colleagues to ensure the quality, integrity and regulatory compliance of our studies and their results. We also conduct complex exploratory analyses, by applying novel statistical methodologies to answer critical healthcare questions and to fully understand our clinical trial data. 

**Who You Are**

* Pursuing a degree in Mathematics, Data Science, Bioinformatics, Computer Science, Statistics, or a related quantitative field
* Knowledge and understanding of basic statistics, with an interest in developing your statistical skills further
* Knowledge and experience programming in R or SAS (among other languages) beneficial
* Comfortable working as part of teams consisting of both technical and non-technical colleagues

# **Function: Real World & Clinical Data Strategy**

The Real-World & Clinical Data Strategy (RWCDS) team at Roche develops and implements  data strategies that unlock the value of clinical, operational, and real-world data to accelerate drug development and evidence generation. We are offering positions in 2 areas within RWCDS:

## **Role: Data Steward**

Data Stewards ensure that clinical and real-world datasets are documented, accessible, trustworthy, and findable by assisting with provenance tracking, defining metadata, and cataloging datasets. Working across operational, clinical trial, and real-world data, they produce interactive catalogue entries, aligned and standard data dictionaries that enable scientists to locate and reuse data, while ensuring compliance with data privacy and security regulations such as HIPAA and GDPR.

## **Role: Data Strategy & Analytics Specialist**

The Data Strategy & Analytics Specialist (DSAS) designs and executes data analyses to support decision-making while translating complex scientific and research questions into structured data requirements. They work with multi-modal data spanning clinical trials, operational metrics, and real-world data to produce analysis reports or dashboards alongside mapped technical specifications for clinical use cases.

The Quantitative Clinical Pharmacology department within pRED, which is outside of the PD organisation but supports projects through both early and late stages, requiring strong collaboration with our PD colleagues.  Our aim is to select the safest, efficacious dose and dosing schedule through analysis of pharmacokinetic (PK), pharmacodynamic (PD), efficacy and safety data. Clinical Pharmacology Data Scientists (CPDS) supports the Quantitative Clinical Pharmacology department by creating ready to use analysis datasets, providing graphical evaluation of the data and conducting exploratory analysis. We work closely with Clinical Pharmacologists to analyse and report data from clinical studies. We are thrilled to invite ambitious graduate candidates who would like to build a career in **Salesforce** to apply for the **next cohort** of our **EMEA Graduate Rotation Program - Sales Path.**  
  
This exciting **12-month program** is designed to give graduates exposure to both sales and solution engineering. Having built the foundational skills for both roles and met our eligibility criteria, top graduates on this path can begin their **Salesforce Sales** careers. The promotion window opens from **month 7 onwards.**  
  
 Our graduate program is a fully immersive experience, combining comprehensive learning paths with in-role experience. By joining Salesforce, you will have the opportunity to lay the foundation for a **fast-paced, successful career.** We are a proud member of the **Fortune 100 Best Places to Work** list for the past 14 years and a consistent winner of **Great Place to Work** awards.

* You are goal-oriented and comfortable in a fast-paced environment

**What does our EMEA Graduate Program look like?**

**Introduction Month**

  

During your first month, you will receive extensive onboarding enablement through a Salesforce-style academy, where you will:

* Become immersed in the culture of Salesforce and gain a deep understanding of our values
* Develop an understanding of our solutions, technologies, and tools
* Learn critical professional skills for your career at Salesforce
* Follow a structured learning calendar with sessions and hands-on workshops led by experts and program alumni

This is an opportunity to take ownership of some of sees.ai’s most important international customer relationships as we move from successful trials towards large-scale operational use across Europe.

We are about to begin rolling out our service with a major French electricity transmission operator. Successfully introducing a new operational capability into an organisation of this scale requires more than delivering the technology.

The customer needs to understand where the value lies, how the service fits into its wider operation and what successful adoption looks like. Different stakeholders will have different priorities, and the scope of the relationship will continue to develop as both organisations learn more.

You will become the senior owner of that relationship, while helping sees.ai develop and manage similar relationships with infrastructure operators across Europe.

Working directly with senior customer stakeholders, you will help define the business case for each phase of these relationships, establish how success will be measured and ensure that customers can see the value sees.ai is creating.

You will work alongside our Client Delivery, Operations, Engineering and Commercial teams to turn those customer objectives into something sees.ai can deliver credibly and commercially.

**Details: -**

**Location: London (hybrid), with regular travel to our Chichester office, France and elsewhere in Europe  
Reports to: VP of Customer Success  
Essential: Fluent spoken and written French and English**

## 

The context

Energy grids worldwide are under enormous pressure from rising demand, ageing infrastructure and the transition to renewable generation. Operators need more frequent, consistent and detailed information about their networks than conventional inspection methods can provide.

sees.ai collects and delivers that information safely and at scale using autonomous UAS.

Today, the data primarily consists of high-resolution imagery, with the capability extending to video, thermal imaging and LiDAR. We develop the entire system in-house: the UAS, ground-control systems, cloud software and field operation itself.

Our work with National Grid in the UK has already progressed from trials into full operational service. France is our first major expansion market beyond the UK and represents the next important stage of our international growth.

This role will help shape and support that rollout, while developing the customer relationships that will underpin sees.ai’s broader expansion across Europe.

* Become sees.ai’s senior relationship owner for key European customers, beginning with a major French electricity transmission operator moving into operational rollout.
* Work with customers to define the business case, outcomes and measures of success for each stage of the relationship.
* Translate emerging customer needs into clear briefs, working with Client Delivery, Operations and Engineering to ensure that sees.ai’s response is credible and deliverable.

* Manage the transition of relationships from sees.ai’s existing senior stakeholders, then build and lead the Customer Success team required as our European customer base grows.

Essential skills and experience

* Fluent spoken and written French and English, with the ability to lead executive meetings, workshops and commercial discussions in both languages.
* Significant experience owning and growing complex, high-value enterprise customer relationships.
* Experience working with senior stakeholders inside large, complex or highly regulated organisations.
* A track record of developing a business case or commercial brief collaboratively with a customer.

* The ability to work effectively alongside Delivery, Operations, Product and Engineering without blurring ownership or making commitments on their behalf.

* Experience building and leading teams.
* Willingness to travel regularly to France and elsewhere in Europe.

Desirable skills and experience

* Experience helping customers adopt a new operational technology or service at scale.
* Experience in a growing technology company where roles, processes and customer propositions are still developing.
* Familiarity with autonomous systems, UAS, data services, inspection technology or other operational technologies.
* Experience introducing Customer Success governance, reporting or account-management systems from the ground up.
* Additional European language skills.

What success will look like

* Our customer has a clear and evidenced business case for moving from trial into wider operational use.
* Senior customer relationships transfer successfully from sees.ai’s existing stakeholders without losing momentum or trust.
* Customer Success and Client Delivery have clearly defined and effective responsibilities.

* New opportunities across Europe are identified, assessed and converted into well-defined areas of work.

At Semble, we are on a mission to enable health professionals to amplify their impact. # Experiential Marketing Lead (Head of Shopify Spaces, London)

* Remote - United Kingdom
* Creative

## About the role

We believe brand is built in the moments people remember, and few moments stick like being in the room. Events are among the hardest things in marketing to attribute and among the easiest to remember. Nobody decides to start a business because of an ad. They decide because they met someone, heard something, tried something, or saw what was possible up close. We want Shopify to be where that happens.

Shopify is coming to London with its first permanent London Space: a hub for the people turning ideas into companies, side hustles into million-pound brands, and local communities into global commerce movements. On the surface, this will be a beautiful room where Shopify hosts founder talks, product education, retail pop-ups, product launches, and cultural moments. The real job is more interesting: make the Space proof that the future of commerce is already happening here.

Our New York Space has shown what happens when commerce and culture are woven together: 100K+ annual visitors, high-signal brand and creator activations, and moments people keep talking about after they leave, from celebrity-founder pop-ups to tent-pole activations around Marathon Weekend and Fashion Week. London deserves its own version, not a copy/paste of what we have already done. It needs someone with the taste and nerve to make it feel unmistakably of the city.

We’re hiring a Head of Spaces, London to build the experiential program strategy for the Space and run the room: programming, production, community, operations, team, partners, and the culture and quality bar. Your work will help entrepreneurs in London become more successful, make Shopify’s role in retail commerce impossible to miss, and turn the Space into a brand channel that travels far beyond the people who were there in person.

If your instinct is to maximize the calendar, this will be a frustrating role. If your instinct is to ask what people will still be talking about in a month, it will not.

# What you’ll do

* **Build the London strategy for Shopify Spaces.** Define the programming thesis, roadmap, budget, KPI model, and operating cadence for a Space whose job is to make Shopify unmistakably useful and culturally relevant for London entrepreneurs, retailers, creators, and commerce communities.
* **Make the case for why Spaces matter.** Turn the London Space into a strategic asset for Shopify: a place where entrepreneurs get more successful, our role in retail and commerce becomes tangible, and the brand earns attention because the work is useful, surprising, and worth sharing.
* **Build the system, not just the calendar.** Establish how ideas are sourced, briefed, greenlit, produced, marketed, measured, and, when they are not strong enough, killed.
* **Act as curator-in-chief.** Be the gatekeeper for only “hell yes” opportunities. Program a mix of pop-ups, founder salons, product education, retail experiments, community dinners, workshops, talks, launches, and cultural moments that feel inevitable, not busy.
* **Make London feel like London.** Stay close to the founders, retailers, creatives, agencies, communities, neighbourhoods, and brands shaping commerce in the city. Spot the people worth backing before they are obvious.
* **Produce moments people repeat.** Own the end-to-end experience with your team, including the tiny details people remember without knowing why. The work should be strong enough in the room and interesting enough to travel on social afterwards.
* **Use the product, not just the logo.** Make Shopify’s commerce platform visible in retail experiments and pop-up infrastructure, from Point of Sale to Shop App moments like geo-gated drops, merchant storytelling, inventory, payments, and checkout.
* **Build the team.** Hire, manage, and develop the soon-to-be-built London Spaces team, including senior event producers, event operations, and partnership marketing roles.
* **Own the partner and vendor ecosystem.** Establish and manage relationships with experiential agencies, freelancers, fabricators, AV teams, caterers, staffing partners, security, and local collaborators who determine whether an idea survives contact with reality.
* **Run the machine.** Own the practical reality of a permanent Space, including budgets, security, storage, AV, maintenance, rituals, and operating standards that keep the Space sharp every day.
* **Measure what actually matters.** Attendance, qualified community growth, pipeline influence, product engagement, partner value, and earned attention all matter. So do the harder-to-measure moments that make people feel inspired, connected, and more likely to build with Shopify.

# What we’re looking for

* **Founder-grade experiential judgement.** You have built events, spaces, festivals, pop-ups, communities, or cultural programs where the stakes were real and the details mattered. You know because you have done it, not because you supervised from a distance.
* **Taste, demonstrably.** A body of work you can point to, defend, and critique honestly.
* **Cultural fluency in London.** You know when to show up and when to sit out. You understand where entrepreneurs, retailers, creators, and communities actually gather, not just where trend reports say they do.
* **Production fluency.** Credibility with the vendors and partners who make the work real. You can speak confidently with fabricators, AV teams, caterers, staffing partners, agencies, security, and landlords.
* **Systems thinking.** You can hold a three-year ambition and a broken microphone in the same afternoon. You build the process that lets creative work scale without sanding off its edge.
* **Senior influence.** You can advise executives and make a case with sharp reasoning rather than consensus theatre.
* **Operational nerve.** You are calm inside complexity and can make order out of chaos.
* **Curious about commerce and technology.** You do not need to be a Shopify expert on day one. You do need to care about entrepreneurs, retail, culture, and the pace of change in commerce.

This role probably is not for you if your strongest work is executing someone else’s event brief inside an established machine. We need someone who can design the operating system for a new Space, set a high creative bar, know which opportunities deserve a hard no, and still break the pattern when the right idea comes along.

# Practical details

* This is a hybrid London-based role. Expect to spend more time on site in year one while building out the strategy, operating rhythm, and team.
* At full operation, expect to work from the London Space approximately three days a week, with flexibility around major activations.
* Some programming will happen at night or on weekends. This is part of the role.
* Occasional travel may be required.

# How to apply

No cover letters. Send a CV or portfolio link if it helps us understand your work. In the application below, we're going to ask these two questions. These questions are about taste, cultural understanding, and how you see London.

1. **Who would make the line go around the block?** Name one relatively unheard-of London-based brand, business, creator, founder, community, or shop you would partner with for the Space. What would you build with them, who would come, and why should Shopify be the one to host it?
2. **Where do London entrepreneurs actually hang out?** We’re new to London. Give us a short map, list, voice note, deck, or memo of the physical places, rooms, shops, studios, communities, and neighbourhoods we should understand before opening. Tell us the five you would visit first and why.

## About Shopify

Opportunity is not evenly distributed. Shopify puts independence within reach for anyone with a dream to start a business. We propel entrepreneurs and enterprises to scale the heights of their potential. Since 2006, we’ve grown to over 8,300 employees and generated over $1 trillion in sales for millions of merchants in 175 countries.

This is life-defining work that directly impacts people’s lives as much as it transforms your own. This is putting the power of the few in the hands of the many, is a future with more voices rather than fewer, and is creating more choices instead of an elite option.

## About you

Moving at our pace brings a lot of change, complexity, and ambiguity—and a little bit of chaos. Shopifolk thrive on that and are comfortable being uncomfortable. That means Shopify is not the right place for everyone.

Before you apply, consider if you can:

* Care deeply about what you do and about making commerce better for everyone
* Excel by seeking professional and personal hypergrowth
* Keep up with an unrelenting pace (the week, not the quarter)
* Be resilient and resourceful in face of ambiguity and thrive on (rather than endure) change
* Bring critical thought and opinion
* Put AI agents and tools to work on the tasks they're built for, and focus on the work only humans can do
* Embrace differences and disagreement to get shit done and move forward
* Work digital-first for your daily work

*We may use AI-enabled tools to screen, select, and assess applications. All AI outputs are reviewed and validated by our recruitment team.*

We are currently selecting an advanced scheduling platform to support this. The analytical foundation underneath it,how we measure productivity, what our labour standards are, how good our demand forecasts need to be - is what this role owns.

You will sit in the Data team and work in close partnership with FP&A. **Job Purpose:**

As the Obsolescence Process Manager, you are primarily responsible for establishing and operating a proactive, auditable obsolescence-management process across the product lifecycle. You will monitor component, material, and supplier lifecycle status; assess technical, commercial, quality and programme risks; and coordinate timely, cost-effective mitigation to protect production continuity, product supportability and customer commitments. The role works closely with Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, Operations and Programme, Project & Product Management, using a plan to prioritise and close open obsolescence issues.

  

**Main Responsibilities**:

  

* Own and maintain the company obsolescence-management process, governance, procedures, registers and Obsolescence Management Plans, aligned with contractual requirements and recognised good practice such as IEC 62402.
* Monitor bills of material, approved parts, materials for lifecycle risk using supplier notices, product change notifications, end-of-life notices, market intelligence and approved lifecycle tools.
* Maintain accurate ERP, PLM and obsolescence-system data attributing to role, including lifecycle status, affected products, risk ratings, owners, actions, due dates and supporting evidence.
* Assess the impact of each issue on safety, compliance, quality, configuration, cost, inventory, schedule, production continuity, product supportability and customer commitments.
* Coordinate cross-functional investigations and recommend proportionate mitigation, including authorised alternate sources, form-fit-function substitutes, last-time or lifetime buys, repair, redesign, technology refresh or controlled product phase-out.
* Assist preparation of robust business cases and technical recommendations, balancing lifecycle demand, total cost, lead time, minimum order quantities, storage life, qualification effort and residual risk.
* Work with Engineering, Quality and Programme Management to ensure replacement solutions are appropriately evaluated, qualified, approved and implemented through formal change control processes.
* Work with wider Supply Chain team to receive timely lifecycle information, validate notices, identify alternatives and improve the quality and timeliness of obsolescence data.
* Chair regular Obsolescence Review Meetings; communicate priorities, decisions, dependencies and escalations; and drive actions through to verified closure.
* Develop and report key performance indicators covering exposure, ageing, response time, mitigation status, cost avoidance, residual risk and data quality.
* Support new product introduction, sourcing and design reviews by promoting lifecycle-aware component selection, second-source strategies and long-term availability considerations in conjunction with wider Supply Chain team.
* Ensure proposed mitigations comply with applicable quality, regulatory, environmental, export-control, customer, counterfeit-avoidance and traceability requirements.
* Provide training, guidance and continuous improvement to embed proactive obsolescence ownership across relevant functions and perform other duties or special projects as assigned.

  

**Education/ Qualifications:**

**Knowledge and Experience:**

* Experience of obsolescence, DMSMS, component engineering, product lifecycle, through-life support or technical supply-chain management.
* Knowledge of electronic, electromechanical or mechanical components and their lifecycle risks
* Experience interpreting bills of material, engineering drawings, specifications, supplier notices and lifecycle data.
* Understanding of ERP/MRP and PLM systems, configuration control and engineering change processes.
* Experience of risk assessment, technical investigations, mitigation planning and supplier engagement.
* Knowledge of IEC 62402, counterfeit avoidance, REACH, RoHS and aerospace or defence quality requirements.

  

**Competencies**:

  

* Strong analytical, data-management and problem-solving skills.
